Definition: adverb from a derivative of G3551; legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists):--lawfully.
BiblicalUsage: Lawfully is the way the law is to be used, and the way the race is to be run. Paul says the law is good if a man uses it lawfully, and the athlete is not crowned unless he strives lawfully — the rules are not the enemy, they are the course.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lawful use is the whole art: the law is good when it is used as law, and the crown goes to the one who runs by the rules.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
